definitions.explanation: Holding a post, seat, or membership on an ongoing, permanent basis rather than temporarily. Used attributively before the name of a position or organization.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}はこのオーケストラの{常任|じょうにん}{指揮者|しきしゃ}だ。
examples.english: He is the permanent conductor of this orchestra.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}は{常任|じょうにん}{理事国|りじこく}を{目指|めざ}している。
examples.english: Japan is aiming to become a permanent member state.

examples.japanese: {常任|じょうにん}{委員会|いいんかい}のメンバーとして、{毎週|まいしゅう}の{会議|かいぎ}に{出席|しゅっせき}している。
examples.english: As a member of the standing committee, I attend the weekly meetings.

notes:
Almost always used attributively (before a noun), not as a standalone predicate. It marks a role as ongoing and fixed rather than temporary or rotating.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {常任|じょうにん}{理事国|りじこく}: permanent member state (of the UN Security Council)
- {常任|じょうにん}{指揮者|しきしゃ}: permanent/principal conductor
- {常任|じょうにん}{委員会|いいんかい}: standing committee
- {常任|じょうにん}{理事|りじ}: standing director

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {常勤|じょうきん}: full-time — refers to working hours, not to the permanence of a post
